title: Interaction skeletons and choropleth token library for cost heatmaps
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Design a compact set of interaction skeletons (stateful micro-patterns) and a dedicated choropleth token palette for rendering cost heatmaps across Console dashboards and rollout views. Provide Figma components, token mappings, and accessibility contrast guidance for engineering handoff.
background: Cost heatmaps and region/lens tiles have grown organically across the Console. Multiple teams ship slightly different color ramps, hover states, and loading skeletons which causes inconsistent density perception and inaccurate rollup visualizations. This ticket consolidates a design system artifact that teams can adopt for consistent heatmap semantics, reduced cognitive load, and measurable accessibility improvements.
goals: Create a single token set (choropleth ramp + neutral anchors) for Console cost visualizations
Define interaction skeletons for tile loading/empty/error states with animation guidance
Produce Figma components and variants for heatmap legends, tile overlays, and micro-tooltips
Document contrast and accessible thresholds for color ramps and state icons
Deliver developer-friendly token mapping and CSS variable names for runtime themes
acceptance_criteria: Figma library published with components and token page (choropleth-1..7, anchor-1..3, overlay-alpha)
Design spec doc in Confluence describing mapping from design tokens -> CSS variables -> runtime feature flags
Prototype (iframe) demonstrating hover, focus, loading skeleton, and error states for tiles
Accessibility checklist passed: WCAG AA contrast for static labels and 3:1 for non-text UI components
Sign-off from PM: Cost Views, and Engineering owner for Console rendering pipeline
decisions: Use a seven-step diverging-ish choropleth with a neutral midpoint for mixed credit/debit views
Keep skeleton animation subtle (20% opacity shimmer, 400ms loop) to avoid motion sickness
Expose tokens as semantic names (token.heat.very-low .. token.heat.very-high) rather than raw hex values
feedback_notes: PM review (2026-03-02): prefer fewer steps for micro-tiles; reduced palette variants for compact views
Engineering review (2026-03-04): requested explicit CSS var naming and a fallback grayscale ramp for print/PDF exports
Accessibility review (2026-03-06): flagged mid-point anchor contrast for small captions; adjusted anchor luminance by +6%
Design critique (2026-03-09): asked to add token aliases for Dedicated/private branding overrides
next_steps: Incorporate engineering CSS variable suggestions into token page
Publish Figma library v0.3 and tag consuming teams
Create a short rollout plan and QA checklist for Console-heatmap adoption
Schedule 30m handoff session with ENG rendering and PM Cost Views
notes: 2026-02-17: initial exploration sketches created; compared three ramp families (sequential, diverging, categorical)
2026-02-25: prototype built in Figma with interactive components; early perf concerns noted for heavy tile counts
2026-03-01: handoff doc drafted with suggested batching knobs for rendering library
